name: r2-all-1
statement: The RL-Zero-Math delta acts through the coherent sign pattern of its entries along high-curvature (high on-policy Fisher) directions, roughly 700 times more consequential per unit norm than a random direction, and not through which entries are large; so any unbiased resampling of it (DARE, either half of the tensors) keeps the gain until the injected noise's KL, about (1-q)/(q*rho) times the delta's own, outgrows it, magnitude-ranked neurons do no better than random ones, the same magnitudes with random signs do nothing, and a low-leverage imitation (SFT) delta breaks under the same sparse copy.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800): partial, resampled, sign-altered and ranked copies of the weight delta, scored on MATH-500 at the n13 setting (plain chat prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, one sample) under grader v3, and teacher-forced KL on stored answers; the 1B bytegraft SFT delta as the low-leverage contrast. It does not cover the cue, temperature or sampling results, which behaviour the delta encodes, or the points RL holds over the cued base.

explains.quote: DARE's realized change energy is 33 to 1,000 times the whole delta's
explains.how: Random-direction noise has about 1/700 of the delta's curvature per unit norm, so even 1,000x the energy (q = 0.1 %) adds only about 1.4x the delta's KL, which accuracy tolerates.

explains.quote: Top minus random -1.8 to +3.4, smallest BH p 0.107
explains.how: The effect sits in signs and cross-coordinate structure, not in large weights, so the most-changed neurons carry only their proportional share.

explains.quote: RL minus its top set: 90.4-91.6 (not necessary)
explains.how: Removing the largest-magnitude entries removes almost none of the sign-coherent push, so RL keeps its accuracy.
Magnitude ranking selects entries whose share of the curvature-weighted effect is close to their share of entries, as magnitude alignment near 1 predicts.
Attribution (gradient times delta) is sign-aware and finds 3x more of the effect than a sign-blind magnitude ranking.

explains.quote: 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score
explains.how: Nearly every neuron's delta is aligned in sign with the descent direction of KL to RL: a coherent sign pattern spread over all neurons.

explains.quote: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger)
explains.how: The SFT delta is large and, by the imported leverage table, of low sign coherence (rho_sign < 6), so it is the regime where DARE damage (1-p)/(p*rho) explodes.
On a low-leverage fine-tune delta the sparse rescaled copy injects noise far larger than the delta's effect and destroys the model, as the damage law predicts.
Math-RL and Code-RL share the update mask (set by the base) but not the signs; for math, the Code delta is close to a sign-randomized delta, so its math effect should be near zero.

conflicts.how: At 10 % the magnitude ranking closes twice the random share, so magnitude carries some information; the theory needs this to come from the correlation of magnitude with sign reliability (sub-ulp entries have noisy signs).

conflicts.quote: a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain
conflicts.how: On a cap-limited Qwen 0.8B a directionless edit helped; the theory says a norm-matched random edit on Olmo carries 1/700 of the delta's KL and should do nothing, so this must be specific to a model with 95 % cap hits.
If the signs of rounding-level changes are noise, the true sign coherence is lower than a uniform reading suggests, which would make DARE fail at a larger q than predicted here.

rival: Low-rank function, high-rank noise (r1-surprises-2), or the published reading of Fisher sparsity (2609.36262) that the effect sits on high-Fisher coordinates with large updates. Separation: (1) a Fisher-weighted magnitude ranking (sum of F_ii * d_i^2 per neuron) is sign-blind: the Fisher-coordinate rival predicts it approaches the attribution ranking (about 13 %), this theory predicts it stays near the weight-change ranking (about 5 %). (2) The sign-only copy sign(d) * mean|d| keeps signs and erases magnitude and much of the singular structure: this theory predicts near-RL accuracy, the low-rank rival predicts a large loss. (3) DARE at q = 0.01 %: this theory predicts collapse; a 'noise is harmless at any energy' reading of the n13 plateau predicts about 430.

predictions.experiment: Base + sign-randomized RL delta (every tensor; each entry keeps |d| and gets a random sign), plain chat prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, MATH-500 n=500, one sample, grader v3 (endpoints v3: base 305, RL 464)
predictions.refuted_by: 345 or more right (a delta with the right magnitudes and random signs gives a real gain)

predictions.experiment: Base + sign-only delta: in every tensor, each changed entry set to sign(d) * (mean |d| over that tensor's changed entries), unchanged entries left at 0; same setting
predictions.refuted_by: 385 or fewer right (signs alone do not carry the gain)

predictions.experiment: n13 DARE arm at q = 0.01 %: base + MLP delta entries kept with probability 1e-4 and scaled by 10,000, attention and norms from base; same setting
predictions.refuted_by: 300 or more right (the DARE plateau continues to q = 0.01 %)

predictions.experiment: Teacher-forced on the 80 stored MATH-500 answers of result-156f7b: RL model with its MLP delta replaced by a DARE copy; mean per-token KL(arm || RL) at q = 0.1 % divided by the same at q = 1 %
predictions.refuted_by: ratio below 5 or above 20 (noise KL does not scale as (1-q)/q)

predictions.experiment: cleanneurons Part T protocol with a sign-blind Fisher-weighted ranking: neuron score = sum over its entries of F_ii * d_i^2, F_ii the base's diagonal Fisher on its own 40 cued T1 answers (no RL labels); top 1 % of MLP neurons copied from RL; share of KL(RL||base) closed on the 40 held-out T1 answers at the decisive positions
predictions.refuted_by: 11 % or more (a sign-blind curvature ranking approaches the sign-aware attribution ranking's 13.7 %)

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas, Fisher curvature along the delta is about 708x that of a same-norm random direction (SFT 5.5); the effect sits in signs and cross-coordinate structure (sign-flip null loses it, magnitude alignment about 1); DARE damage follows (1-p)/(p*rho_sign).
imports.how: Turns the team's two unexplained DARE facts (RL survives 1,000x noise energy; the bytegraft SFT delta goes to 0/1,200) into one quantitative law, and predicts a cliff below q = 0.1 %, a null sign-flip arm, a near-RL sign-only arm and a sign-blind Fisher ranking no better than magnitude.

imports.finding: DARE's output change is bounded by Psi(p)/(1-p) times the mean and variance of delta-times-activation terms; DARE fails on large deltas and at high drop rates.
imports.how: Explains why the 100x larger Think-SFT and bytegraft deltas are in the failing regime while the 0.24 %-of-norm RL delta is not, and sets the scale at which the RL DARE plateau must end.
